title: Asking for the bill; tú vs usted
summary: Ask for the bill, answer card/cash questions, and pick tú or usted with the right verb form.
prereqText: Review lesson 1 (greeting-and-ordering) if you cannot yet order a drink with por favor.

exemptions.worked: The worked function is replaced by the guided dialogue and the verb-form decision walkthrough in the explain and classify blocks; there is no multi-step procedure beyond choosing a form, which the decision visual models.

blocks.html: You have finished your coffee and tostada. The waiter is busy at the other end of the bar. You want the bill. Then he glances over and asks you something, using either quieres or quiere. Which one is he using, and which should you use back?
Think of tú and usted as two volume knobs for closeness: tú is close and relaxed, usted is respectful or distant. Two dials in your head: Who is this person to me? and How formal is the place?
blocks.limits: It is not a strict rule and it varies by region, age, venue and the speakers' own habits. Learners cannot read all of those cues yet, so you need a safe default and a way to follow the other person's lead.

blocks.purpose: Show how to decide between tú and usted from simple cues, and what each choice does to the verb.
blocks.alt: A decision diagram. Start: someone addresses you or you address someone. If they used tú with you, you may use tú. If they used usted, use usted. If unsure, use usted. Usted uses the verb form quiere; tú uses quieres.

blocks.title: Bill phrases and the two forms of 'you'
blocks.html:
The bill. La cuenta, por favor. is the standard polite request. Other options: ¿Me cobras, por favor? (tú) / ¿Me cobra, por favor? (usted), and ¿Cuánto es? (How much is it?). The waiter may ask ¿Efectivo o tarjeta? (cash or card?). You answer Con tarjeta or En efectivo. You may ask ¿Puedo pagar con tarjeta? (Can I pay by card?). Status: the phrases are standard beginner Spanish; I could not verify them against the DLE or Plan curricular (sources unavailable).

What the forms are. Tuteo means addressing someone as tú. For querer (to want): tú quieres, usted quiere. Fact (secondary source, fetched): usted means 'you' but takes third-person singular verb forms, for example puede usted sentarse.

Which to use? Honest status: the Spanish Wikipedia article on tuteo says tú is the most widespread informal form in Spain, but that sentence has no inline citation. I found no primary-source statement about café service specifically. Course decision (not a documented rule): waiters and customers in casual bars often use tú with each other, and usted is common with older people or in more formal venues. These are generalisations, so do not treat them as universal.

Practical guidance for you. (1) If someone addresses you as usted or tú, answer in the same form. (2) If unsure, usted is the safer default for a stranger who is clearly older or in a formal place. (3) Por favor and gracias work in both. (4) Plural in much of central and northern Spain: vosotros is informal and ustedes formal (secondary source); you only need to recognise these at A1.

blocks.prompt: The waiter asks: "¿Qué quieres tomar?". Which form of 'you' is he using with you?

feedback.1: Usted would take the third-person verb: ¿Qué quiere tomar?
feedback.2: You can tell: quieres (ends in -s) is the tú form of querer.

blocks.explanation: Quieres = tú. The -s ending marks the second-person singular. Since he used tú, you may reply with tú forms too.

blocks.instructions: Sort each sentence by the form of address it uses: informal (tú) or formal (usted). Look at the verb ending first.
blocks.debrief: The cue is the verb: -s (quieres, pones, cobras) = tú; no -s (quiere, pone, cobra) = usted. Le/te are object pronouns that also signal the form: le = usted, te = tú.

items.feedback: Quiere: third person form, so usted.
Te is the tú object pronoun.
Le is the usted object pronoun.

config.debrief: Both forms are polite in context; usted adds distance or respect.

blocks.instructions: Complete each question with the verb form that matches the person addressed (given in brackets after the sentence).
blocks.debrief: Check the pairing: tú → quieres, usted → quiere. The same -s test works for many verbs.

config.text:
Friend your age (tú): ¿Qué [[quieres::querer]] tomar?

Older waiter you want to be formal with (usted): ¿Qué [[quiere::querer]] tomar?

Asking a waiter you address as tú: ¿Me [[cobras::cobrar]], por favor?

Asking a waiter you address as usted: ¿Me [[cobra::cobrar]], por favor?

blocks.instructions: Read the dialogue. Answer the comprehension questions. Then type how you would ask for the bill and how you would answer the card/cash question.
blocks.debrief: Here the waiter uses usted (¿Le cobro?). Notice you do not need to use any verb at all to ask for the bill: La cuenta, por favor works with both forms.

What does the waiter ask about payment?
options: Whether you want to pay later

feedback.0: Receipt = ticket / recibo, not in this dialogue.

production.tips: La cuenta, por favor is the safest phrase because it needs no choice between tú and usted.

production.prompt: Answer "¿Efectivo o tarjeta?" saying you pay by card.
production.tips: Con = with / by. For cash: en efectivo.

blocks.task: Compute this illustrative bill, then say it in Spanish: 2 cafés at 1.60 € each and 1 tostada at 2.20 €. Write the total in numbers and in Spanish words (euros con céntimos).
rubric: Says it as 'cinco euros con cuarenta'
blocks.solution: 5.40 € → cinco euros con cuarenta. (Prices are illustrative.)

blocks.task: With your friend: they play a waiter. Round 1: they use usted (¿Qué quiere tomar? / ¿Le cobro?). Round 2: they use tú (¿Qué quieres tomar? / ¿Te cobro?). You order, ask for the bill, say cash or card, and each time answer in the same form they used.
rubric: Understood both forms of the waiter's question
Switched forms correctly when your friend switched
blocks.externalFeedback: Ask your friend to note when your form of address did not match theirs, and whether any phrase sounded stiff or too casual for a bar. They represent one speaker's habits, not all of Spain. The app cannot evaluate speech.
blocks.model: La cuenta, por favor. — ¿Efectivo o tarjeta? — Con tarjeta. Gracias.

questions.prompt: A much older waiter in a traditional café says "¿Qué desea?". You are not sure whether to use tú or usted with him. A reasonable choice is…
options: avoid all verbs and never use por favor

feedback.1: Convenience is not a social reason; when unsure, usted is the safer default.
feedback.2: Por favor works in both forms; dropping it makes you sound rude.

questions.explanation: When unsure, usted is the safe default (course decision; he also used a formal-sounding question).

questions.prompt: Complete: "¿Qué ___ tomar?" addressed to a waiter you call usted.
questions.explanation: Usted takes the third person singular: quiere.

questions.prompt: Which phrase asks for the bill without choosing tú or usted?
questions.explanation: No verb that marks the form.

questions.prompt: Illustrative prices: 2 cañas at 2.50 € each and 1 tortilla at 3.00 €. Total in euros?
In your own words: how do you choose between tú and usted in a café, and what is the verb difference?
rubric: Says to follow the other person's form or default to usted when unsure
questions.model: Copy the form the other person uses with you; if unsure, use usted. Tú: quieres; usted: quiere.

blocks.task: New context: you are in a small hotel breakfast room and the manager (a woman in her sixties) asks if you want anything else, then you want to settle the bill for the room's drinks. Write: (a) how you reply when she asks "¿Desea algo más?", (b) how you ask her for the bill, and (c) which form of address you choose and why.
rubric: Replies with a polite short answer (nada más, gracias)
Chooses usted, with a reason (older, formal setting, unsure)
blocks.model: (a) Nada más, gracias. (b) La cuenta, por favor. (c) Usted: she is older and the setting is formal; I do not know her.

blocks.prompt: Describe a situation where you would still be unsure which form to use. What would you do in that moment?
